stories.text: Cal Ripken Jr. of the world-champion Baltimore Orioles is selected named American League MVP, edging teammate Eddie Murray. Ripken gets 15 first-place votes and 322 points, while Murray garners 290 points and ten first-place nods. Carlton Fisk gets the remaining three top-of-the-ballot votes.

stories.text: Kevin Cash of the Tampa Bay Rays was named American League manager of the year for the 2nd straight year while Gabe Kapler of the San Francisco Giants was named National League manager of the year.

stories.text: On November 16, 2019, Citi Field hosted the New York Hurling Classic—a one-day hurling tournament featuring Limerick, Kilkenny, Tipperary, and Wexford for the Players Champions Cup—which was won by Kilkenny.

stories.text: Miami Marlins CEO Derek Jeter unveiled a new logo, team colors and uniform for the 2019 MLB season. The new design replaced the one used after the club moved to Marlins Park in 2012, and switched from the Florida Marlins to the Miami Marlins.
stories.headline: Derek Jeter Unveils New Miami Marlins Logo and Uniforms
stories.extract: Derek Sanderson Jeter, nicknamed "the Captain", is an American former professional baseball player, businessman, and baseball executive. A shortstop, Jeter spent his entire 20-year Major League Baseball (MLB) career with the New York Yankees. He was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility…

He played for the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim and Pittsburgh Pirates of Major League Baseball from 2007 through 2011. He managed the Tri-City Dust Devils of the Low-A Northwest League in 2016.

He was a member of the Pittsburgh Pirates from 1986 to 1992 and the San Francisco Giants from 1993 to 2007. Bonds is widely considered to be one of the greatest baseball players of all time.

stories.text: The Colorado Rockies sign free agent first baseman Andrés Galarraga, who rejoins Don Baylor, his hitting coach with the St. Louis Cardinals. Galarraga is coming off his second injury-plagued year, having missed 44 days of the season after being hit on the wrist by a Wally Whitehurst pitch in the third game of the season.
stories.headline: Rockies Sign Andrés Galarraga, Reunite With Don Baylor

stories.text: The Giants sign outfielder Kevin Bass, a former NL All-Star, granted free agency from the Houston Astros three days ago.
stories.headline: Giants Sign Former NL All-Star Kevin Bass
stories.extract: Kevin Charles Bass is an American former professional baseball right fielder who played in Major League Baseball for the Milwaukee Brewers (1982), Houston Astros, San Francisco Giants (1990–1992), New York Mets (1992), and Baltimore Orioles (1995).

stories.text: José Canseco is the unanimous choice as the American League Most Valuable Player, winning all 28 first-place votes cast. Canseco led the AL in homers (42), RBI (124) and slugging (.569), and also stole 40 bases in 1988. He becomes the Junior Circuit's first consensus MVP since another Oakland outfielder, Reggie Jackson, in 1973.
stories.headline: José Canseco Unanimous AL MVP, Winning All 28 First-Place Votes
stories.extract: José Canseco Capas Jr. is a Cuban-American former professional baseball outfielder and designated hitter who played 17 seasons in Major League Baseball (MLB). During his time with the Oakland Athletics, he established himself as one of the premier power hitters in the game. He won the Rookie of the Year (1986), and…

stories.text: The Chicago Cubs steal a crucial free agent from their South Side rivals, when the parent Tribune Company's WGN-TV signs Harry Caray as their play-by-play broadcaster away from the White Sox. Already a legend over his 37-year career, which began as the voice of the Cubs' NL arch-rivals, the St. Louis Cardinals, Caray, now 67, has been the star of the White Sox' radio/TV booth since 1971.
stories.headline: Cubs Sign Harry Caray Away From White Sox for WGN-TV

stories.text: Rod Carew of the Minnesota Twins easily beats Al Cowens of the Kansas City Royals and Ken Singleton of the Baltimore Orioles to win the 1977 American League MVP Award.
stories.headline: Rod Carew Beats Cowens and Singleton to Win AL MVP
stories.extract: Alfred Edward Cowens, Jr. was an American right fielder in Major League Baseball. From 1974 through 1986, Cowens played for the Kansas City Royals (1974–79), California Angels (1980), Detroit Tigers (1980–81) and Seattle Mariners (1982–86). He batted and threw right-handed.

stories.text: Roberto Clemente of the Pittsburgh Pirates (202 hits, 29 HR, 119 RBI, and a Gold Glove right fielder in 1966) is selected the Most Valuable Player of the National League by the BBWAA. The future Hall-of-Famer is the first Puerto Rican and second Latin American to capture an MLB MVP award.
stories.headline: Roberto Clemente Named NL MVP, First Puerto Rican to Win

On December 31, 1972, Clemente was killed when his Douglas DC-7 airplane, which he had chartered for a flight to deliver…

stories.text: Principal owner Louis R. Perini sells the Milwaukee Braves to a syndicate headed by Chicago businessman William Bartholomay for a reported $5.5 million. Perini originally bought into the Braves in 1944, when they were based in his home city of Boston, then moved them to Milwaukee in 1953.
stories.headline: Perini Sells Milwaukee Braves to Bartholomay Syndicate for $5.5 Million

image.alt: Black-and-white halftone portrait of a middle-aged man in a suit.

stories.extract: The Milwaukee Braves were a Major League Baseball team that played in Milwaukee, from 1953 to 1965, having previously played in Boston, Massachusetts, as the Boston Braves. After relocating to Atlanta, Georgia in 1966, they were renamed the Atlanta Braves. The 13-season tenure in Milwaukee at Milwaukee County Stadium…

stories.text: Chicago White Sox owner Grace Reidy Comiskey announces that her son, Chuck Comiskey, who turns 30 in three days, and son-in-law Johnny Rigney, 41, an ex-ChiSox pitcher, both vice presidents, will share baseball-operations duties formerly performed by Frank Lane, who quit as general manager two months earlier.
stories.headline: Comiskey, Rigney to Share White Sox Baseball Operations Duties
stories.extract: Grace Elizabeth Reidy Comiskey was an American businesswoman who was the owner of the Chicago White Sox of the American League from 1939 through 1956. Comiskey was the daughter-in-law of Charles Comiskey and inherited control of the White Sox upon the death of her husband, J. Louis Comiskey.

stories.text: Future Hall-of-Fame slugger Ralph Kiner becomes a "player to be named later" in an earlier (September 30) transaction when the Chicago Cubs ship him to the Cleveland Indians as part-payment for pitcher Sam "Toothpick" Jones. The trade will conclude on November 30 when the Cubs receive outfielder Gale Wade (also a "PTBNL") and $60,000 from Cleveland.
stories.headline: Ralph Kiner Traded to Indians as Player to Be Named Later
stories.extract: Ralph McPherran Kiner was an American professional baseball left fielder in Major League Baseball (MLB) and later a broadcaster. Kiner played for the Pittsburgh Pirates, Chicago Cubs, and Cleveland Indians from 1946 through 1955.

stories.extract: George Howard "Jake" Northrop nicknamed "Jerky", was an American pitcher in Major League Baseball. He played for the Boston Braves.

stories.text: Eddie Plank reportedly jumps from the Philadelphia Athletics of the American League to the Federal League's Chicago Federals after Athletics owner Connie Mack instigates a fire sale, asking waivers for Plank, Jack Coombs, and Chief Bender.
stories.headline: Plank Jumps From Athletics to Federal League Chicago Federals

stories.text: The joint rules committee drops the 4-strike experiment from 1887 and returns to the standard 3-strike rule. The committee also drops the base on balls as counting for a hit in official statistics.
stories.headline: Rules Committee Drops 4-Strike Rule, Returns to Three Strikes

stories.text: The joint rules committee between the National League and the American Association announce the new rules for the 1887 season which include 5 balls for a walk, 4 strikes for an out, the batter calling for pitch location being abolished and establishing a strike zone between the knees and shoulders of the batter.
stories.headline: Joint Committee Sets 5 Balls for Walk, 4 Strikes for Out
